newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Era GSM to increase investment in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Era GSM to increase investment in 1997.

text.p: Era GSM, one of Poland's three cellular telephone operators, plans to increase its investment in 1997 from last year's levels, its general manager said on Monday.
"In 1996 we surely invested some $200-$300 million and we want to increase the amount in 1997," Tadeusz Kubiak told Reuters after a news conference. He declined to give more specific figures.
He said Era GSM, which opearates a modern digital GSM system, had attracted 40,122 customers since launching operations in September last year.

The cellular phone market's leader -- PTT Centertel, which has been active since 1991 -- has more than 150,000 customers. But analysts say Centertel, operating the older analog system, is eventually doomed to lose the race for customers.
Era's other competitor is Polkomtel SA, which also runs a GSM system.
Era's shareholders include Polish trading and industrial conglomerate Elektrim with a 32.5 percent stake, and US West and Deutsche Telekom's subsidiary DeTeMobil holding 22.5 percent stakes each.
